source_title: Rurouni Kenshin: Every Saga, Ranked From Worst to Best - GameRant
source_excerpt:
Cathlyn is an anime writer with years of experience covering some of the biggest and most popular series of all time. She loves writing listicles, features, and query-based articles about all things related to anime. Outside of writing, she enjoys playing mobile games, building Lego and Nanoblock sets, playing pickleball, watching movies, and rewatching her favorite anime series. Before joining GameRant as a contributor, she worked in Epicstream’s anime department. Beyond her passion for anime, she also enjoys writing romance fiction, with her most successful work surpassing one million reads on Wattpad.
Kenshin Himura embarks on a long and bloody journey in Rurouni Kenshin . Everywhere he goes, trouble follows, as his brutal past as the legendary Battousai continues to haunt him, no matter how badly he wants to abandon it. It's almost as if there's no escape from the enemies who seek revenge or the bloodshed he desperately hopes to leave behind.
That said, Kenshin's journey is divided into several story arcs, each one forcing the former assassin to wield his unique weapon. It goes without saying that these Rurouni Kenshin story arcs put Kenshin in difficult situations that test his swordsmanship, challenge his vow never to kill again, and force him to confront the consequences of his bloody past.
10 The Feng Shui Arc Strays Too Far From Rurouni Kenshin's Roots
The Feng Shui Arc is a five-episode filler storyline that throws the Kenshingumi into a conflict between the rival Water and Wind Clans. Kenshin joins forces with Jinpuu, the last mystic of the Wind Clan, to take on the Water Clan's Reisui and Yusui. What ensues is a battle involving ancient mysticism, supernatural abilities, and a struggle for power that tests Kenshin and his allies in an entirely different way.
The Feng Shui Arc leans more heavily into fantasy than other Rurouni Kenshin storylines, making it feel out of place in a series centered on swordsmanship and historical conflicts. Unfortunately, its focus on mystical powers and rival clans also leaves the Kenshingumi feeling disconnected from the main conflict. It comes as no surprise that the arc struggles to hold viewers' attention, with several dull episodes that lack the compelling story found in stronger arcs.
9 The Black Knights Arc Gives Western Knights a Place in Kenshin's World
In this arc, the Kenshingumi face off against the Black Knights, led by First Lieutenant Meldars, a skilled fighter who excels at mounted combat with his platinum lance. The group seeks to obtain the Divine Elixir and monopolize its production to develop cures, ultimately hoping to seize control of Japan. Meanwhile, Misanagi, the leader of the Sanada Clan, becomes entangled in the conflict, unaware that her clan is merely a pawn in Meldars' ambitious plans.
The Black Knights Arc is another short filler storyline that spans just six episodes. Despite its brevity, it explores some intriguing ideas, particularly the clash between samurai and Western knights, with Kenshin struggling against armored opponents. The arc also features surprisingly compelling antagonists, including Schneider, whose sense of justice makes him a memorable filler character. That's not all, as the contrast between modern Western ideals and feudal Japan also adds a unique touch to the storyline.
8 The Katsu Kaishu Arc Is a Short Filler With a Few Bright Spots
The Katsu Kaishu Arc is a short filler storyline that spans just four episodes. Unlike most arcs in Rurouni Kenshin , it shifts much of the focus away from the Kenshingumi and instead follows the father and daughter duo of Katsu Kaishu and Itsuko . The two find themselves caught up in a dangerous conflict with the Beni-Aoi, a criminal gang that is after Tokugawa Yoshinobu's money.
While the Katsu Kaishu Arc features an interesting storyline with a few twists and turns, it pales in comparison to other filler arcs. Still, it has its share of entertaining moments, particularly the exciting fight between Kenshin and Tetsuma, which adds some much-needed action to the otherwise short storyline.
7 The Pirate Shura Arc Brings Pirates and Sword Fights to Rurouni Kenshin
The Pirate Shura Arc is the first anime-original arc in the 1996 Rurouni Kenshin adaptation. Although relatively short, it delivers an entertaining adventure as Kenshin and his friends encounter a notorious group of pirates known for hijacking ships. Led by the fierce Shura, the Kairyu targets a ship belonging to Senbonya Yohei, which Kenshin and his allies are tasked with protecting.
Their encounter soon escalates into a confrontation between the wandering swordsman and the ruthless pirates. Despite being a filler arc, the Pirate Shura Arc receives a generally positive reception for its exciting fights, not to mention memorable characters, especially Shura, who could have been an alternate love interest for Kenshin.
6 The Shimabara Arc Is a Surprisingly Strong Rurouni Kenshin Filler Arc
There's plenty to love about the Shimabara Arc, from its historical touch and engaging storyline to its memorable cast of fleshed-out characters. Among them are the siblings Amakusa Shogo and Sayo, whose actions and Christian beliefs leave a profound impact on Kenshin and Sanosuke, making this anime-original arc a worthwhile addition to the Rurouni Kenshin series.
Kenshin's battle against Shogo also lives up to expectations, as the two swordsmen clash using their respective versions of the Amakakeru Ryu no Hirameki techniques, resulting in an intense showdown that tests their swordsmanship and resolve. Despite being enemies, the two swordsmen shared a deep understanding of each other, adding emotional depth to their otherwise fierce rivalry.
5 The Hokkaido Arc Brings Kenshin Back for One More Adventure
As fans know, the Hokkaido Arc picks up Kenshin's story after the events of the original manga, following his life as a devoted husband and father. In this direct sequel, Kenshin, Kaoru, and their new companions journey to Hokkaido in search of Kaoru's father, who was supposed to have been dead.
To this day, the Hokkaido Arc remains divisive among fans. While some were excited to see Kenshin embark on a new adventure, others believed the Jinchu Arc provided a satisfying conclusion to his story. Regardless, the Hokkaido Arc has plenty of exciting developments in store, from formidable new enemies and intense sword fights to fresh challenges that test Kenshin and his allies.
4 The Tokyo Arc Brings Together Action and Everyday Adventures
The Tokyo Arc welcomes viewers to the dangerous world of Rurouni Kenshin , introducing the main characters, Kenshin, Kaoru, Sanosuke, and Yahiko. Obviously, it's not as intense as the other story arcs in the series, but it still features intense fights that Kenshin usually wins with little to no difficulty. That doesn't mean there are no skilled opponents in this arc, as it still features the likes of Udo Jin-e and Shinomori Aoshi.
In addition, the Tokyo Arc has plenty of laid-back moments where the characters bond with one another, giving viewers a glimpse of their everyday lives. At the same time, the story arc relies on a "villain of the week" formula, introducing new antagonists who challenge Kenshin before the story moves on to its next conflict.
3 The Remembrances Arc Explores the Heartbreaking Past of the Hitokiri Battousai
The Remembrances Arc is another essential part of Kenshin's story, offering a deeper look into his bittersweet past. Through his recollections, Kenshin reveals to the Kenshingumi his former life as the Hitokiri Battousai, shedding light on the difficult experiences that shaped him into the wandering swordsman he is today.
Taking place through flashbacks during the Jinchu Arc, this storyline explores Kenshin's life before the revolution, including his time as an assassin and the crucial events that ultimately lead him to abandon killing. In particular, the arc excels in its portrayal of romance through Kenshin and Tomoe's heartbreaking love story.
2 The Jinchu Arc Turns Kenshin's Past Into His Greatest Threat
Without a doubt, the Jinchu Arc is one of the most integral story arcs in Rurouni Kenshin . Not only does this major arc reveal the true reason behind Kenshin's no-killing vow, but it also pushes him to his mental, emotional, and physical limits. The intense struggles he faces take a serious toll on his psyche, bringing him to the brink of madness.
It goes without saying that fans shouldn't skip the Jinchu Arc, as it provides crucial insight into Kenshin's past, present, and future. Of course, the fights are just as incredible, with Kenshin and his allies facing the vengeful Enishi and highly skilled comrades who are out to lay siege to the Kamiya dojo.
1 The Kyoto Arc Sets an Almost Impossible Standard
The Kyoto Arc is widely regarded as one of the best story arcs in Rurouni Kenshin , largely due to the presence of Makoto Shishio, the ruthless assassin who replaces Kenshin Himura as the government's man-slayer. Betrayed by the government and left to burn alive, Shishio survives and returns with a thirst for revenge, leading a formidable group of rogue swordsmen who threaten to plunge Japan into chaos.
For the first time in the series, Kenshin takes the threat seriously, knowing that he must face Shishio in a life-or-death battle that only he can finish. The arc features an exciting buildup as Kenshin and his allies grow stronger in preparation for the inevitable clash. The arc also introduces Kenshin's master, whose training proves crucial to Kenshin's climactic fight with Shishio . In general, the Kyoto Arc features an exceptional storyline that's incredibly difficult to surpass due to its peak writing, satisfying fights, and unforgettable, charismatic characters.
